findings.title: Insufficient permission check in resolve method
findings.explanation: The `resolve` method permits the ticket reporter to resolve a ticket and completely ignores the `admins` parameter, allowing users who should not have permission (reporters) to resolve tickets and preventing administrators from doing so, violating the intended access control. Also reported by compliance, defects as requirement_mismatch: The code permits the reporter to resolve tickets and does not check administrators, violating the requirement that only the assignee or an administrator may resolve a ticket.

finding.title: Rule: Public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise
finding.explanation: The newly added public method `resolve` has a one-line docstring, but it only mentions the raised PermissionError and does not describe what the function returns (a Ticket). This violates the rule that the docstring must state what the function returns or raises.

evidence.quote: """Mark a ticket resolved. Raises PermissionError if `actor` is not allowed to."""
Public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise.

dismissed.reason: The rule requires the docstring to state what the function returns or raises; the docstring already mentions the raised PermissionError, satisfying the "or raise" condition, so the claim of violation is not supported.
